fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. Numbers 3:4 says Nadab and Abihu died in the presence of the LORD because of "unauthorized fire" in the Wilderness of Sinai. I think this is a heavy moment, and I'm not going to joke about it. The text tells us plainly what happened, so I'll leave it right there.

Judges were a real job in Israel's story later on (Judges 2:16), but that's not what this verse says. Numbers 3:3 says Aaron's sons were "…the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests." The word is priests, anointed and ordained. Nobody here is banging a gavel.

Yes, friend. Numbers 3:8 says the Levites "…shall take care of all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting…" Not some of them, all of them. That's a lot to be trusted with, and I get nervous just thinking about the inventory.

The sea parting is a real event (Exodus 14:21), but it isn't what the LORD points to here. In Numbers 3:13 He says, "On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to Myself all the firstborn in Israel…" That's the day He means.

The stone tablets are real (Exodus 31:18), but they aren't what this verse is about. Numbers 3:13 says, "On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to Myself all the firstborn in Israel…" The day in Egypt is the one the LORD points back to.

That's it, friend. Moses, Aaron and Aaron's sons camp on the east, toward the sunrise. Numbers 3:38 says they do the duties of the sanctuary as a "service on behalf of the Israelites." Their work isn't for themselves. It's for the people.

Gate duty? I can picture it, friend, a little vest and a flashlight. But that's not on the list. Numbers 3:38 says Moses, Aaron and Aaron's sons were to perform "…the duties of the sanctuary as a service on behalf of the Israelites…" The sanctuary is the job.

True, friend. The LORD tells Moses, "You are to take the Levites for Me—I am the LORD—in place of all the firstborn of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites." (Numbers 3:41). So the instruction covers the animals too, not just the people.

Look at the end of that verse, friend. The LORD says to take the Levites for Him "…and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites." (Numbers 3:41). So His instruction includes the livestock right alongside the people.

Five shekels, friend. The LORD says, "…you are to collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs." (Numbers 3:47). Same price for each one, no haggling, and He even names which shekel to use. If only every bill came that clear.

Thirty shekels shows up elsewhere in the Bible (Exodus 21:32), but not here. The LORD says, "…you are to collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs." (Numbers 3:47). For these 273, the price is five.

Sons, that's the one. The LORD says, "Give the money to Aaron and his sons…" (Numbers 3:48). So the whole priestly household is on the receiving end. Moses collects it, then hands it over, just as Numbers 3:51 says.

Elders don't show up in this verse, friend. The LORD says, "Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the excess among the Israelites." (Numbers 3:48). Those are the two names He gives for where this money goes.
